title: FAUST: XVIII. Evidence of annular substructure in a very young Class 0 disk
question: Does the very young Class 0 disk around Oph A SM1 show annular substructure (gap or ring) in 3 mm dust continuum, and is the emission at that location optically thin?

recipe.goal: Calibrate, self-calibrate and image the 3 mm continuum
recipe.method: Self-calibration of C-10 and C-6 separately, then combined, with multiscale then mtmfs cleaning
key_parameters: Combined data averaged to 9 s and 30 MHz channels
assumptions: Primary beam response at SM1 is 0.35 because the field target was VLA 1623-2417

recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fit to the 3 mm emission to get centre, inclination (circular geometry) and PA

recipe.goal: Build the deprojected radial intensity profile in brightness temperature
recipe.method: Deproject with the fitted geometry, azimuthally average, express as brightness temperature with the full Planck function; error sigma_std/sqrt(N)
key_parameters: brightness temperature calculated using the full Planck function

recipe.goal: Fit smooth, gap and ring models to the intensity profile
recipe.method: Beam-convolved models fitted with emcee; log of model and data used in the likelihood to weight fractional errors
key_parameters: 50 walkers, max 300,000 steps, stop when steps > 100x autocorrelation time and autocorrelation estimate varied < 1%
burn-in twice the autocorrelation time, thinning half the autocorrelation time
assumptions: Gap and ring each modelled as a Gaussian annular feature

recipe.method: Akaike Information Criterion; lowest AIC favoured; difference >~10 taken as significant

recipe.goal: Measure the intra-band spectral index profile
recipe.method: Image lower- and upper-sideband spectral windows separately with the same imaging parameters, build intensity profiles and compute alpha = ln(I1/I2)/ln(nu1/nu2)
key_parameters: alpha constrained only within ~30 au (beyond that below 3 sigma)

recipe.goal: Derive dust temperature and 3 mm optical depth
recipe.method: Modified blackbody fit of the 106 and 94 GHz profiles; in the optically thick inner region temperature equals brightness temperature; outside r~15 au temperature extrapolated with a -0.5 power law
key_parameters: temperature at gap/ring about 15/13 K, tau(3 mm) below 1
assumptions: Passive heating profile T ~ r^-0.5 beyond ~15 au

recipe.goal: Estimate disk mass and protostar luminosity limit
recipe.method: M_disk = 2 pi integral Sigma r dr with Sigma = tau/kappa; constant tau_3mm = 8 inside ~15 au, R = 40 au; luminosity from temperature scaling T ~ (phi L)^(1/4)/r^(1/2)
assumptions: kappa(3 mm) ~ 1 cm2/g and gas-to-dust ratio 100
Temperature difference to other embedded disks is due only to luminosity (similar flaring, irradiation heating only)

recipe.goal: Predict 1.3 mm intensity and optical depth
recipe.method: Extrapolate tau_3mm to 1.3 mm with constant beta between 1 and 1.7, using the derived temperature profile; also test an inclination of 60 deg
assumptions: Inclination of 60 deg raises optical depth by a factor of about 2

recipe.goal: Estimate possible planet mass from gap width
recipe.method: Gap width relation from Kanagawa et al. (Eq. 4), cross-checked against Rosotti et al. simulations
assumptions: Protostar mass of 1 Msun (unknown); planet mass scales linearly with it
